CyberCloud.Analytics/clickhouseClusters.title: ClickHouse cluster
CyberCloud.Analytics/clickhouseClusters.summary: A managed ClickHouse cluster on the Altinity operator, with declared shards and replicas and a ClickHouse Keeper quorum. The schema is the tenant's.

fields.name: location
fields.label: Location
fields.hint: The region the cluster is billed in.
fields.disabledReason: This value cannot change after the resource is created. Create a new ClickHouse cluster to change it.

fields.name: properties
fields.label: Properties
fields.hint: The cluster's own settings.

fields.name: clusterId
fields.label: Cluster id
fields.hint: The cluster whose namespace holds the ClickHouse cluster.
fields.disabledReason: This value cannot change after the resource is created. Create a new ClickHouse cluster to change it.

fields.name: keeperNodes
fields.label: Keeper nodes
fields.hint: Number of ClickHouse Keeper nodes. Keeper is a Raft quorum, so three is the smallest count that survives losing one and an even count tolerates no more failures than the odd count below it. One is offered for development and has no quorum at all.

fields.name: monitoring
fields.label: Monitoring
fields.hint: What the platform scrapes.

fields.name: enabled
fields.label: Enabled
fields.hint: Whether ClickHouse's own Prometheus endpoint is served on port 9363. On by default — docs/plan/12: "a managed service the tenant cannot see the health of is a black box they will not trust with production". ⚠ It makes the metrics exist; the object that scrapes them is not built — see conformance.yaml § owed.

fields.name: replicas
fields.label: Replicas
fields.hint: Number of replicas per shard. This is the availability axis, and it only applies to tables the tenant creates as Replicated — the resource does not manage tables. Total server count is shards times replicas.

fields.name: shards
fields.label: Shards
fields.hint: Number of shards. This is the capacity and parallelism axis: a table's data is split across shards and a query fans out to all of them. ⚠ Resharding an existing table is not something the operator or this resource does, so growing this moves new data only.

fields.name: sizing
fields.label: Sizing
fields.hint: CPU and memory per ClickHouse server, either by preset or explicitly. The Keeper nodes are sized by the platform and are not affected.

fields.name: cpu
fields.label: Cpu
fields.hint: Explicit vCPU quantity in Kubernetes form, for example 500m or 2. Empty means take it from the preset.

fields.name: memory
fields.label: Memory
fields.hint: Explicit memory quantity in Kubernetes form, for example 8Gi. Empty means take it from the preset.

fields.name: preset
fields.label: Preset
fields.hint: A sizing preset from docs/plan/12. Analytics uses the m1 family, which is 1 vCPU to 8 GiB.

fields.name: storage
fields.label: Storage
fields.hint: The data volume, per ClickHouse server.

fields.name: class
fields.label: Class
fields.hint: StorageClass name for the ClickHouse servers and the Keeper nodes. Empty means the cluster default.
fields.disabledReason: This value cannot change after the resource is created. Create a new ClickHouse cluster to change it.

fields.name: size
fields.label: Size
fields.hint: Data volume size per ClickHouse server, in Kubernetes quantity form. Grows online; never shrinks.

fields.name: version
fields.label: Version
fields.hint: ClickHouse version, which is also the ClickHouse Keeper version — the two share a release train and a wire protocol. Only long-term-support lines are offered; a new api-version is what adds a third.

fields.label: Tags

fields.name: properties
fields.label: Properties
fields.hint: The cluster's own settings.

fields.name: clusterId
fields.label: Cluster id
fields.hint: The management cluster the control plane runs in. ⚠ This is not the cluster being created: it is the cluster whose API server accepts the Cluster API objects that create one.
fields.disabledReason: This value cannot change after the resource is created. Create a new Managed Kubernetes cluster to change it.

fields.name: controlPlane
fields.label: Control plane
fields.hint: The control plane, which runs as pods in the management cluster.

fields.name: replicas
fields.label: Replicas
fields.hint: How many copies of the API server, controller manager and scheduler to run. Two survives a node failure; one is offered for development. ⚠ Unlike an etcd quorum this is a plain replica count — the datastore is separate and is shared — so an even number is not the mistake it would be on a Raft member set.

fields.name: monitoring
fields.label: Monitoring

fields.name: enabled
fields.label: Enabled
fields.hint: Whether the control plane's own metrics endpoints are scraped. On by default — docs/plan/12: "a managed service the tenant cannot see the health of is a black box they will not trust with production". ⚠ It covers the control plane, which runs in the management cluster. Nothing scrapes inside the cluster being created; that needs an agent in the bundle.

fields.name: network
fields.label: Network

fields.name: podCidr

fields.name: serviceCidr
fields.label: Service cidr

fields.disabledReason: This value cannot change after the resource is created. Create a new Managed Kubernetes cluster to change it.

CyberCloud.ContainerService/managedClust.title: Node pool
CyberCloud.ContainerService/managedClust.summary: A group of identically sized worker virtual machines in a managed Kubernetes cluster, optionally under a cluster-autoscaler.

fields.name: location
fields.label: Location
fields.hint: The region the pool is billed in.
fields.disabledReason: This value cannot change after the resource is created. Create a new Node pool to change it.

fields.name: properties
fields.label: Properties
fields.hint: The pool's own settings.

fields.name: autoscale
fields.label: Autoscale
fields.hint: Whether a cluster-autoscaler may resize the pool.

fields.name: enabled
fields.label: Enabled
fields.hint: Whether the pool carries autoscaler bounds. Off by default. ⚠ Turning it on changes what the pool costs: quota is then reserved against maxCount, because a pool that may grow to twenty machines has to have twenty machines' worth of headroom to grow into.

fields.name: maxCount
fields.label: Max count
fields.hint: The largest the autoscaler may grow the pool to, and what quota is reserved against while autoscaling is on. ⚠ Nothing checks that it is at least minCount — that is a relation between two properties of one body, which the schema validates nothing about.

fields.name: minCount
fields.label: Min count
fields.hint: The smallest the autoscaler may shrink the pool to. Ignored when autoscaling is off.

fields.name: clusterId
fields.label: Cluster id
fields.hint: The management cluster the machine objects are applied to. Must be the one the cluster is in — nothing checks that, and a pool placed elsewhere produces a MachineDeployment naming a Cluster that is not there, which Cluster API accepts and never reconciles.
fields.disabledReason: This value cannot change after the resource is created. Create a new Node pool to change it.

fields.name: count
fields.label: Count
fields.hint: How many worker VMs the pool runs. ⚠ When autoscaling is on this is the starting size and the autoscaler moves it; quota is reserved against the maximum in that case, not against this.

fields.name: osDiskSize
fields.label: Os disk size
fields.hint: The root volume of each VM, in Kubernetes quantity form. It holds the operating system, the container images and every writable layer, so a pool running large images needs more of it than a pool running small ones.
fields.disabledReason: This value cannot change after the resource is created. Create a new Node pool to change it.

fields.name: size
fields.label: Size
fields.hint: The VM size, from the platform's sizing catalogue. Kubernetes nodes use the s1 family, which is 1 vCPU to 4 GiB. ⚠ Immutable: a Cluster API machine template cannot be resized in place, so changing this would mean replacing every VM in the pool, which is a different operation from the one a PUT looks like.
fields.disabledReason: This value cannot change after the resource is created. Create a new Node pool to change it.

fields.name: upgrade
fields.label: Upgrade
fields.hint: How machines are replaced when the pool changes.

fields.name: maxSurge
fields.label: Max surge
fields.hint: How many extra machines may exist during a rolling replacement. One means a new VM boots and joins before an old one is removed, which is why it is the default: it costs one machine's capacity and loses none.

fields.name: maxUnavailable
fields.label: Max unavailable
fields.hint: How many machines may be missing during a rolling replacement. Zero with a surge of one is the safe pair; raising it is faster and reduces the pool's capacity while it runs. ⚠ Both being zero would make an upgrade unable to start, and nothing refuses that pair.

fields.name: version
fields.label: Version
fields.hint: The Kubernetes minor version the nodes run. ⚠ It may be up to three minors behind the cluster's control plane and may never be ahead of it. This API does not check that — the cluster's version is a different resource — so an illegal pair is accepted here and produces nodes that join and then misbehave.

fields.label: Tags
fields.hint: Key/value tags, at most 50 pairs — docs/plan/06 § Tags, locks. Values are strings; the cap applies to the merged set, so a PATCH that adds one tag to a full bag is refused.

CyberCloud.Messaging/kafkaClusters.title: Kafka cluster
CyberCloud.Messaging/kafkaClusters.summary: A managed Apache Kafka cluster on Strimzi in KRaft mode, with Cruise Control, configurable retention and an optional firewalled external listener.

fields.name: location

fields.disabledReason: This value cannot change after the resource is created. Create a new Kafka cluster to change it.

fields.name: properties
fields.label: Properties

fields.name: cruiseControl
fields.label: Cruise control

fields.name: listener

fields.name: monitoring

fields.name: retention
fields.label: Retention

fields.name: hours
fields.label: Hours
fields.hint: Default retention in hours. A week by default.

fields.name: size
fields.label: Size

fields.name: sizing
fields.label: Sizing

fields.name: memory

fields.name: storage

fields.name: class

fields.name: size

fields.name: topics
fields.label: Topics

fields.name: minInSyncReplicas

fields.name: partitions
fields.label: Partitions

fields.name: replicationFactor

fields.name: version

fields.name: jetstream

fields.name: leafNodes

fields.name: limits

fields.name: servers

fields.name: sizing

fields.name: storage

CyberCloud.Messaging/rabbitmqClusters.summary: A managed RabbitMQ cluster on the RabbitMQ Cluster Operator, with quorum queues as the default queue type and the management UI reachable only in-cluster.

fields.name: location
fields.label: Location
fields.hint: The region the cluster is billed in.
fields.disabledReason: This value cannot change after the resource is created. Create a new RabbitMQ cluster to change it.

fields.name: properties
fields.label: Properties
fields.hint: The cluster's own settings.

fields.name: clusterId
fields.label: Cluster id

fields.name: limits
fields.label: Limits
fields.hint: Broker limits a client can run into.

fields.name: maxMessageSize
fields.label: Max message size
fields.hint: Largest message a client may publish, in bytes. Raising it costs memory on every node that holds a copy, which for a quorum queue is all of them.

fields.name: nodes
fields.label: Nodes
fields.hint: Number of RabbitMQ nodes. Use an odd number of at least three: a quorum queue is a Raft group, so a group of two tolerates no failures and an even count buys nothing over the odd count below it. One is offered for development only and replicates nothing.

fields.name: plugins
fields.label: Plugins

fields.name: additional
fields.label: Additional
fields.hint: Plugins to enable on top of the three the operator always enables — peer discovery, the management UI and the Prometheus endpoint. Each recognised plugin adds its own port to the cluster's in-cluster Service.

fields.name: queues
fields.label: Queues
fields.hint: How queues behave when a client does not say.

fields.name: defaultType
fields.label: Default type
fields.hint: The queue type a client gets when it declares a queue without asking for one. Quorum by default — docs/plan/12: a quorum queue is replicated through Raft across the nodes above, and on 4.x a classic queue is not replicated at all, so leaving this unset would put a single-node queue on a cluster the tenant paid three nodes for. fields.name: sizing
fields.label: Sizing
fields.hint: CPU and memory per node, either by preset or explicitly.

fields.name: cpu
fields.label: Cpu
fields.hint: Explicit vCPU quantity in Kubernetes form, for example 500m or 2. Empty means take it from the preset.

fields.name: memory

fields.name: preset
fields.label: Preset
fields.hint: A sizing preset from docs/plan/12. Brokers use the c1 family, which is 1 vCPU to 2 GiB and guaranteed rather than burstable.

fields.name: storage
fields.label: Storage
fields.hint: The message store, per node.

fields.name: class
fields.label: Class

fields.disabledReason: This value cannot change after the resource is created. Create a new RabbitMQ cluster to change it.

fields.name: size
fields.label: Size

fields.name: version

fields.name: tags

CyberCloud.Monitor/workspaces.title: Monitor workspace
CyberCloud.Monitor/workspaces.summary: A tenancy in the platform's metrics, logs and traces stores, with its own retention, quota, ingest key and read-only datasource endpoints.

fields.name: location
fields.label: Location
fields.hint: The region the workspace is billed in, and the region whose telemetry stores hold its data.
fields.disabledReason: This value cannot change after the resource is created. Create a new Monitor workspace to change it.

fields.name: properties
fields.label: Properties
fields.hint: The workspace's own settings.

fields.name: clusterId
fields.label: Cluster id
fields.hint: The regional cluster whose telemetry data plane serves this workspace. ⚠ Nothing is deployed into it: a workspace is a tenancy in stores the platform already runs, and this is where its ingest routing is published.
fields.disabledReason: This value cannot change after the resource is created. Create a new Monitor workspace to change it.

fields.name: purgeProtection
fields.label: Purge protection
fields.hint: Whether this workspace may be destroyed before its seven-day recovery window is out. Once true it stays true for the rest of the workspace's life, and a purge is refused while it is set.

fields.name: quota
fields.label: Quota
fields.hint: What the workspace may take in per day, and what happens when it takes in more.

fields.name: cardinalityCap
fields.label: Cardinality cap
fields.hint: Distinct values one metric label may take before the series carrying it are rejected. The rejection names the offending label — docs/plan/16 § Ingest — because a rejection nobody can diagnose is one the client just retries.

fields.name: logsGbPerDay
fields.label: Logs gb per day
fields.hint: Log lines accepted per day, in gibibytes.

fields.name: metricsGbPerDay
fields.label: Metrics gb per day
fields.hint: Metric samples accepted per day, in gibibytes. This is the first factor of what the workspace draws against the subscription's storage quota; the second is the retention tier.

fields.name: overQuotaSampleRate
fields.label: Over quota sample rate
fields.hint: The percentage of data still accepted once a signal is over its daily allowance. ⚠ It cannot be zero: docs/plan/16 requires that going over quota samples at a visible rate rather than dropping silently, and zero is a silent drop spelled as a rate.

fields.name: seriesCap
fields.label: Series cap
fields.hint: Active metric series the workspace may hold at once. One tenant putting a request id in a metric label is how a shared time-series database dies, so this is a ceiling rather than a guideline.

fields.name: tracesGbPerDay
fields.label: Traces gb per day

fields.name: retention
fields.label: Retention
fields.hint: How long each signal is kept. Priced per tier — docs/plan/16 § Cost and retention honesty.

fields.name: logs
fields.label: Logs
fields.hint: Logs retention tier: short is 7 days, standard 30, extended 90. ⚠ Shortening this under an existing workspace destroys the lines already outside the new window, and the reconciler refuses the change rather than applying it.

fields.name: metrics
fields.label: Metrics
fields.hint: Metrics retention tier: short is 15 days, standard 90, extended 400. ⚠ Shortening this under an existing workspace destroys the samples already outside the new window, and the reconciler refuses the change rather than applying it.

fields.name: traces
fields.label: Traces
fields.hint: Traces retention tier: short is 3 days, standard 14, extended 30. ⚠ Shortening this under an existing workspace destroys the spans already outside the new window, and the reconciler refuses the change rather than applying it.

CyberCloud.Network/publicIpAddresses.title: Public IP address
CyberCloud.Network/publicIpAddresses.summary: A public address allocated from the region's pool, which a load balancer or a gateway can later be given. On its own it carries no traffic.

fields.name: location
fields.label: Location
fields.hint: The region the address is allocated in. ⚠ It must be a region whose operator has an external pool — nothing checks that, and an address in a region with none never becomes ready.

fields.name: properties
fields.label: Properties

fields.label: Address

fields.name: v4
fields.label: V4

fields.name: tags

CyberCloud.Network/virtualNetworks.title: Virtual network
CyberCloud.Network/virtualNetworks.summary: A private routing domain on Kube-OVN with its own address space. Network-layer tenant separation: a private routing domain with its own address space, on shared hardware.

fields.name: tags

CyberCloud.Network/virtualNetworks/secur.title: Security group
CyberCloud.Network/virtualNetworks/secur.summary: A deny-by-default set of allow rules that become OVN ACLs on the ports in a virtual network. A workload may carry several.

fields.name: location
fields.label: Location
fields.hint: The region the security group lives in. It must be the network's own region — nothing checks that.
fields.disabledReason: This value cannot change after the resource is created. Create a new Security group to change it.

fields.name: properties
fields.label: Properties
fields.hint: The security group's own settings.

fields.name: allowSameGroupTraffic
fields.label: Allow same group traffic
fields.hint: Whether workloads that carry this same security group may reach each other without a rule. Off by default: it is the one setting here that permits traffic nobody wrote a rule for.

fields.name: clusterId
fields.label: Cluster id
fields.hint: The cluster whose fabric carries the security group. Must be the cluster the network is in — nothing checks that.
fields.disabledReason: This value cannot change after the resource is created. Create a new Security group to change it.

fields.name: egress
fields.label: Egress
fields.hint: What workloads carrying this group may reach. ⚠ Same default-deny: an empty section permits no outbound traffic at all, which for most workloads means no DNS and no package downloads.

fields.name: allowIcmp
fields.label: Allow icmp
fields.hint: Whether outbound ICMP is allowed to the remotes above. Off by default.

fields.name: remoteV4
fields.label: Remote v4
fields.hint: The IPv4 range outbound traffic may reach, or empty for no IPv4 rules at all.

fields.name: remoteV6
fields.label: Remote v6
fields.hint: The IPv6 range outbound traffic may reach, or empty for no IPv6 rules at all.

fields.name: tcpPorts
fields.label: Tcp ports
fields.hint: TCP ports outbound traffic may reach, in the same form as the inbound list. Empty means no outbound TCP.

fields.name: udpPorts
fields.label: Udp ports
fields.hint: UDP ports outbound traffic may reach. Empty means no outbound UDP — which includes DNS on port 53.

fields.name: ingress
fields.label: Ingress
fields.hint: What may reach workloads carrying this group. ⚠ Anything not allowed here is dropped — the fabric installs a default-deny for every port in a security group, so an empty section permits nothing.

fields.name: allowIcmp
fields.label: Allow icmp
fields.hint: Whether inbound ICMP is allowed from the remotes above. Off by default. ⚠ With this off, a workload in this group does not answer ping and does not receive path-MTU messages.

fields.name: remoteV4

fields.name: remoteV6

fields.name: tcpPorts

fields.name: udpPorts
fields.label: Udp ports
fields.hint: UDP ports inbound traffic may reach, in the same form as tcpPorts. Empty means no UDP is allowed inbound.

fields.name: tags
fields.label: Tags

fields.name: enableDhcp
fields.label: Enable dhcp
fields.hint: Whether the fabric answers DHCP in this subnet. Off by default: an address is assigned to a workload's port when the port is created, and DHCP is for guests that insist on asking — a virtual machine rather than a container.

fields.name: natOutgoing
fields.label: Nat outgoing
fields.hint: Whether workloads in this subnet reach the internet through source NAT. Off by default. ⚠ This is the opposite of Kube-OVN's own default for its cluster subnet, deliberately: a tenant subnet that silently egresses is a surprise, and docs/plan/12 § Cross-cutting decisions defaults external exposure to off. It also requires the network's enableExternal to be on; without it the flag is accepted and nothing egresses.

fields.name: private
fields.label: Private
fields.hint: Whether the subnet refuses traffic from other subnets. Off by default. ⚠ In this api-version it has no exception list, so on means no traffic from any other subnet in the network at all.

fields.name: tags
fields.label: Tags
fields.hint: Key/value tags, at most 50 pairs — docs/plan/06 § Tags, locks. Values are strings; the cap applies to the merged set, so a PATCH that adds one tag to a full bag is refused.

CyberCloud.Search/services.title: OpenSearch service
CyberCloud.Search/services.summary: A managed OpenSearch cluster on the OpenSearch operator, with dedicated cluster-manager, data and optional coordinating node pools and operator-generated transport and HTTP TLS.

fields.name: location
fields.label: Location
fields.hint: The region the service is billed in.
fields.disabledReason: This value cannot change after the resource is created. Create a new OpenSearch service to change it.

fields.name: properties
fields.label: Properties
fields.hint: The service's own settings.

fields.name: clusterId
fields.label: Cluster id
fields.hint: The cluster whose namespace holds the search service.
fields.disabledReason: This value cannot change after the resource is created. Create a new OpenSearch service to change it.

fields.name: coordinatingNodes
fields.label: Coordinating nodes
fields.hint: Number of coordinating-only nodes — nodes that hold no data and no cluster state and exist to fan a search out and merge the results. Zero is the default and is right until a query pattern makes one data node the bottleneck for every search. They are sized by the same preset as the data nodes.

fields.name: dataNodes
fields.label: Data nodes
fields.hint: Number of data nodes. This is the capacity axis: total raw capacity is this count times the disk size below, before replicas. Every data node also carries the ingest role, so an indexing pipeline needs no separate pool.

fields.name: masterNodes
fields.label: Master nodes
fields.hint: Number of dedicated cluster-manager nodes. They hold the cluster state in a quorum, so three is the smallest count that survives losing one. One is offered for development and has no quorum at all. An even count is worse than the odd count below it and the API cannot say so — see the service's own documentation.

fields.name: monitoring
fields.label: Monitoring
fields.hint: What the platform scrapes.

fields.name: enabled
fields.label: Enabled
fields.hint: Whether the operator is asked for a ServiceMonitor. On by default — docs/plan/12: "a managed service the tenant cannot see the health of is a black box they will not trust with production". ⚠ The metrics themselves come from the prometheus-exporter plugin, which the operator installs into every node on the first reconcile after this is turned on — so turning it on restarts the pods and turning it off does not remove the plugin.

fields.name: sizing
fields.label: Sizing
fields.hint: CPU and memory per data node and per coordinating node, either by preset or explicitly. The cluster-manager nodes are sized by the platform and are not affected.

fields.name: cpu
fields.label: Cpu
fields.hint: Explicit vCPU quantity in Kubernetes form, for example 500m or 2. Empty means take it from the preset.

fields.name: memory
fields.label: Memory
fields.hint: Explicit memory quantity in Kubernetes form, for example 8Gi. Empty means take it from the preset.

fields.name: preset
fields.label: Preset
fields.hint: A sizing preset from docs/plan/12. Search nodes use the m1 family, which is 1 vCPU to 8 GiB, because OpenSearch is bound by heap and by the filesystem cache rather than by CPU. The m1 rungs below m1.small are deliberately not offered: OpenSearch derives its JVM heap from the container limit and a node under 4 GiB fails a bootstrap check after passing its readiness probe.

fields.name: storage
fields.label: Storage
fields.hint: The data volume, per data node.

fields.name: class
fields.label: Class
fields.hint: StorageClass name for every node pool. Empty means the cluster default.
fields.disabledReason: This value cannot change after the resource is created. Create a new OpenSearch service to change it.

fields.name: size
fields.label: Size
fields.hint: Disk size per data node, in Kubernetes quantity form. Grows online; never shrinks. The cluster-manager and coordinating nodes get a fixed 10Gi that is not configurable and is counted against the storage quota anyway.

fields.name: version
fields.label: Version
fields.hint: OpenSearch version. ⚠ OpenSearch is a fork of Elasticsearch 7.10 (ADR-011 — Elasticsearch is SSPL and is not available to us) and the two have diverged since, so an Elasticsearch 8 client is not promised anything here. Upgrades between the values below are online and in the maintenance window; a third value is a new api-version.

fields.name: tags
fields.label: Tags
fields.hint: Key/value tags, at most 50 pairs — docs/plan/06 § Tags, locks. Values are strings; the cap applies to the merged set, so a PATCH that adds one tag to a full bag is refused.

CyberCloud.Storage/accounts.title: Storage account
CyberCloud.Storage/accounts.summary: A managed S3-compatible object store on SeaweedFS, with replicated volume servers, a filer and a scalable S3 gateway.

fields.name: location
fields.label: Location
fields.hint: The region the account is billed in.
fields.disabledReason: This value cannot change after the resource is created. Create a new Storage account to change it.

fields.name: properties
fields.label: Properties
fields.hint: The account's own settings.

fields.name: clusterId
fields.label: Cluster id
fields.hint: The cluster whose namespace holds the object store.
fields.disabledReason: This value cannot change after the resource is created. Create a new Storage account to change it.

fields.name: gateway
fields.label: Gateway
fields.hint: The S3 gateway — docs/plan/15's ADR-008: "the API is S3".

fields.name: replicas
fields.label: Replicas
fields.hint: Number of S3 gateway pods. The gateway is stateless, so this is a throughput and availability setting rather than a topology one.

fields.name: masters
fields.label: Masters
fields.hint: Number of master servers. The masters hold the volume topology in a Raft group, so three is the smallest count that survives losing one. One is offered for development and has no quorum at all.

fields.name: monitoring
fields.label: Monitoring
fields.hint: What the platform scrapes.

fields.name: enabled
fields.label: Enabled
fields.hint: Whether the operator is asked for a ServiceMonitor per component. On by default — docs/plan/12: "a managed service the tenant cannot see the health of is a black box they will not trust with production". Turning it off removes the metrics port as well as the scrape, which is the operator's own behaviour rather than this provider's.

fields.name: replication
fields.label: Replication
fields.hint: Where the second copy of every object is placed. None keeps one copy and is for scratch data only. A placement the cluster's topology cannot satisfy leaves volumes read-only rather than failing the create. Immutable, because SeaweedFS applies this to volumes as they are created and never rewrites the ones that already exist — a change would split the account into two durability promises with no way to tell which object got which.
fields.disabledReason: This value cannot change after the resource is created. Create a new Storage account to change it.

fields.name: sizing
fields.label: Sizing
fields.hint: CPU and memory per volume server, either by preset or explicitly. The masters, the filer and the S3 gateway are sized by the platform and are not affected.

fields.name: cpu
fields.label: Cpu
fields.hint: Explicit vCPU quantity in Kubernetes form, for example 500m or 2. Empty means take it from the preset.

fields.name: memory
fields.label: Memory
fields.hint: Explicit memory quantity in Kubernetes form, for example 4Gi. Empty means take it from the preset.

fields.name: preset
fields.label: Preset
fields.hint: A sizing preset from docs/plan/12. Volume servers use the s1 family, which is 1 vCPU to 4 GiB.

fields.name: storage
fields.label: Storage
fields.hint: The data volume, per volume server.

fields.name: class
fields.label: Class
fields.hint: StorageClass name for the volume servers. Empty means the cluster default.
fields.disabledReason: This value cannot change after the resource is created. Create a new Storage account to change it.

fields.name: size
fields.label: Size
fields.hint: Data volume size per volume server, in Kubernetes quantity form. Grows online; never shrinks.

fields.name: version
fields.label: Version
fields.hint: SeaweedFS version. ⚠ SeaweedFS ships a release roughly weekly and maintains no long-term branch, so docs/plan/12's "supported major versions" is a shape this project does not have; the two values here are the two most recent releases and a new api-version is what adds a third.

fields.name: volumeServers
fields.label: Volume servers
fields.hint: Number of volume servers. This is the capacity axis: total raw capacity is this count times the volume size below, before replication.

fields.name: tags
fields.label: Tags
fields.hint: Key/value tags, at most 50 pairs — docs/plan/06 § Tags, locks. Values are strings; the cap applies to the merged set, so a PATCH that adds one tag to a full bag is refused.

CyberCloud.Storage/accounts/buckets.title: Bucket
CyberCloud.Storage/accounts/buckets.summary: An S3 bucket inside a managed object-storage account, with an optional size limit and optional object versioning.

fields.name: location
fields.label: Location
fields.hint: The region the bucket is billed in.
fields.disabledReason: This value cannot change after the resource is created. Create a new Bucket to change it.

fields.name: properties
fields.label: Properties
fields.hint: The bucket's own settings.

fields.name: clusterId
fields.label: Cluster id
fields.hint: The cluster whose namespace holds the bucket. Must be the cluster the account is in — nothing checks that, and a bucket placed elsewhere is applied into a namespace with no object store in it.
fields.disabledReason: This value cannot change after the resource is created. Create a new Bucket to change it.

fields.name: quota
fields.label: Quota
fields.hint: How much the bucket may hold.

fields.name: size
fields.label: Size
fields.hint: The bucket's size limit, in Kubernetes quantity form. Empty means no limit other than the account's own provisioned capacity. ⚠ This is a limit inside capacity the account already reserved; it does not add any, and it is not what the bucket is billed on.

fields.name: versioning
fields.label: Versioning
fields.hint: Whether the bucket keeps previous versions of an overwritten object. Off by default. ⚠ docs/plan/15 § Object storage: SeaweedFS' S3 implementation is "good but not complete" and names object versioning as one of the partial areas, so the supported-operations table for the deployed version — not this property — is what says how completely it behaves.

fields.name: tags
fields.label: Tags
fields.hint: Key/value tags, at most 50 pairs — docs/plan/06 § Tags, locks. Values are strings; the cap applies to the merged set, so a PATCH that adds one tag to a full bag is refused.

CyberCloud.Terminal/consoles.title: Cloud terminal
CyberCloud.Terminal/consoles.summary: A browser shell running in this subscription's own cluster, holding a managed identity, with a persistent home directory and no stored credential.

fields.name: location
fields.label: Location
fields.hint: The region the console is billed in.
fields.disabledReason: This value cannot change after the resource is created. Create a new Cloud terminal to change it.

fields.name: properties
fields.label: Properties
fields.hint: The console's own settings.

fields.name: audit
fields.label: Audit
fields.hint: docs/plan/19 § Auditing. Who, when, from where, which subscription and for how long is always recorded and is not a setting.

fields.name: sessionRecording
fields.label: Session recording
fields.hint: Whether everything typed into and printed by this shell is recorded. ⚠ Off by default and immutable afterwards: a shell contains secrets, a keystroke log is a liability, and a recording that could be switched off mid-life would be worth nothing to the compliance requirement it exists for.
fields.disabledReason: This value cannot change after the resource is created. Create a new Cloud terminal to change it.

fields.name: clusterId
fields.label: Cluster id
fields.hint: The cluster whose namespace holds the shell and its home volume.
fields.disabledReason: This value cannot change after the resource is created. Create a new Cloud terminal to change it.

fields.name: home
fields.label: Home
fields.hint: The persistent home directory. The only part of a console that survives an idle reclaim.

fields.name: retentionDays
fields.label: Retention days
fields.hint: How long $HOME is kept after the console was last attached to. ⚠ Nothing sweeps on it yet — it is carried so that a console created today is swept correctly by whatever does.

fields.name: size
fields.label: Size
fields.hint: The size of $HOME. It grows and never shrinks: a PersistentVolumeClaim refuses a decrease at the API.

fields.name: identity
fields.label: Identity
fields.hint: Who the shell runs as.

fields.name: principalId
fields.label: Principal id
fields.hint: The managed identity every command in this shell acts as. It may not be changed: a console whose identity moved would have an audit trail describing a shell that no longer exists.
fields.disabledReason: This value cannot change after the resource is created. Create a new Cloud terminal to change it.

fields.name: image
fields.label: Image
fields.hint: Which shell image to run.

fields.name: variant
fields.label: Variant
fields.hint: default carries every tool in docs/plan/19's table and takes about 40 seconds to pull cold; minimal carries shells, editors, cyc and kubectl and starts in about 8. The repository and the digest are the platform's.

fields.name: network
fields.label: Network
fields.hint: What the shell may reach. Nothing may ever reach the shell.

fields.name: egress
fields.label: Egress
fields.hint: Internet lets the shell reach public addresses as well as this subscription's own workloads and DNS — a shell that cannot git clone is not a shell. TenantOnly removes the public half and leaves the rest.

fields.name: session
fields.label: Session
fields.hint: When a shell stops. Both numbers are ceilings a tenant may lower and neither may be turned off.

fields.name: idleTimeoutMinutes
fields.label: Idle timeout minutes
fields.hint: How long a shell may sit with nobody typing into it before it is reclaimed. The home volume survives; the pod does not. ⚠ There is no value meaning never — an idle terminal is a tenant paying for something they closed.

fields.name: maxDurationHours
fields.label: Max duration hours
fields.hint: The longest a single shell may run, busy or not. Enforced by the kubelet through the pod's own deadline, so it holds even when nothing of this platform is running.

fields.name: sizing
fields.label: Sizing
fields.hint: CPU and memory for the shell.

fields.name: preset
fields.label: Preset
fields.hint: How much a shell gets. The ladder stops at 2 vCPU and 4 GiB, which is docs/plan/19's ceiling for this row — a workload that needs more needs a cluster and a job rather than a terminal.

fields.name: tags
fields.label: Tags
fields.hint: Key/value tags, at most 50 pairs — docs/plan/06 § Tags, locks. Values are strings; the cap applies to the merged set, so a PATCH that adds one tag to a full bag is refused.
